summary: The Stelato V8 enters the RMB 350,000-class MPV market with a starting price of RMB 319,800, NIO's ES8 deliveries surpass 160,000 units, XPeng posts record Q3 revenue and deliveries, and multiple automakers launch a wave of new models ahead of the Guangzhou Auto Show.

articles.title: Luxeed V8 Launches at ¥319,800, Redefining the Value Benchmark for the 350k-yuan MPV Class
articles.summary: The Luxeed V8 debuts at ¥319,800, entering the premium MPV market with a fully-loaded configuration strategy.
articles.detail: According to NetEase Auto, the Luxeed V8 has officially launched with a starting price of ¥319,800, which the company positions as "the fully-equipped answer for the 350k-yuan MPV class." Amid intensifying competition in the premium MPV segment, the Luxeed V8 enters the market below the ¥350,000 threshold, emphasizing a standard-equipped, full-spec lineup across all trims in an effort to challenge the dominance of models such as the Buick GL8 and Denza D9. The premium MPV segment has been heating up in recent years, with expanding use cases ranging from business reception to large-family travel, making it a key battleground for domestic brands pushing upmarket. The V8's pricing and configuration strategy reflects the brand's aim to quickly build awareness with an "high-spec from the entry level" approach and reduce consumers' decision-making cost. Its market performance will serve as an important test case for assessing the capacity and price sensitivity of the 350k-yuan MPV market.
articles.impact: By entering the 350k-yuan MPV class at ¥319,800, the V8 could trigger a new round of price and feature competition in the premium MPV segment, squeezing the premium margins of joint-venture models.

articles.title: New ES8 Deliveries Surpass 160,000 Units as NIO Pushes for 'Top Premium EV' Title
articles.summary: Cumulative deliveries of the new NIO ES8 have exceeded 160,000 units, further consolidating its position in the premium electric SUV market.
articles.detail: According to NetEase Auto, cumulative deliveries of the new NIO ES8 have surpassed 160,000 units, with the company officially projecting confidence through its positioning as the 'top premium electric vehicle.' As NIO's core model in the large electric SUV segment, the ES8 has continued to invest in product strength, service systems, and its battery-swap network since its generational overhaul. The steady climb in delivery volume validates its appeal in the segment above RMB 350,000. Competition in the premium electric SUV space is intensifying, with rivals such as the AITO M9 and Li Auto L9 continuously drawing away users, yet ES8's ability to maintain delivery growth is closely tied to its differentiated布局 in battery-swap infrastructure, community operations, and smart cockpit experience. The 160,000-unit milestone also means NIO has completed an initial accumulation of brand equity in the premium market, laying the groundwork for future model launches.
articles.impact: Surpassing this delivery scale will strengthen NIO's premium brand pricing power and further validate the viability of the battery-swap model in the large electric SUV market.

articles.title: Xingyue L PLUS Gets 2.0Ti-HEV as Geely's Full Zhiqing Hybrid Lineup Reaches Mass Production
articles.summary: Geely's 2.0Ti-HEV hybrid system launches in the Xingyue L PLUS, completing mass production across the full Zhiqing hybrid lineup.
articles.detail: According to NetEase Auto, Geely's 2.0Ti-HEV hybrid system has officially launched in the Xingyue L PLUS, marking the full-series mass production of its Zhiqing hybrid technology. As the higher-end powertrain option in the Zhiqing hybrid family, the 2.0Ti-HEV balances fuel efficiency with power output, filling Geely's gap in hybrid powertrains for mid-to-large SUVs. As China's hybrid market enters a period of rapid growth, competing technical routes — including BYD's DM-i, Great Wall's Lemon DHT, and Chery's Kunpeng hybrid — are vying in parallel. Geely's full-series coverage through Zhiqing hybrid delivers a complete power matrix spanning sedans to SUVs and entry-level to mid-to-high-end segments. For consumers, hybrid models significantly cut fuel consumption without changing driving habits, making them a key transitional choice for replacing conventional gasoline vehicles.
articles.impact: Full-series hybrid mass production will boost Geely's competitiveness in the mainstream SUV market and accelerate hybrid technology's substitution of comparable pure-gasoline models.

articles.title: XPeng Hits Record Highs in Q3 Revenue and Deliveries, Q4 Output Seen Exceeding 170,000
articles.summary: XPeng posted record highs in both revenue and deliveries in the third quarter, with an optimistic Q4 delivery guidance.
articles.detail: According to NetEase Auto, XPeng's latest quarterly earnings show both revenue and deliveries reaching all-time highs, with Q4 deliveries expected to exceed 170,000 units. The results reflect XPeng's combined progress in product mix optimization, cost control, and the rollout of intelligent driving technology. Volume ramp-up of new models such as the MONA series has opened up a broader mainstream price segment for XPeng, while continued iteration of its XNGP intelligent assisted driving system has reinforced its technology credentials. With the new EV entrants collectively entering a survival-of-the-fittest phase, achieving simultaneous growth in scale and revenue indicates the company is gradually shedding loss pressures and entering a self-sustaining stage. The Q4 delivery expectation of 170,000 units will also keep XPeng near the top of domestic new-EV-maker delivery rankings.
articles.impact: The dual growth in deliveries and revenue will boost capital market confidence and provide another benchmark for the new-EV camp's profitability turning point.

articles.title: Changan CS75 PLUS Blue Whale Edition Posts Real-World Fuel Economy of 3.6L/100km
articles.summary: Real-world tests show the Changan CS75 PLUS Blue Whale edition returning just 3.6L per 100 km, a standout energy performance.
articles.detail: According to NetEase Auto's real-world testing, the Changan CS75 PLUS Blue Whale edition clocked 3.6L/100km in fuel consumption testing, showcasing the technical advantage of the Blue Whale power platform in fuel efficiency. As Changan's self-developed powertrain brand, Blue Whale has continuously optimized energy performance through high-thermal-efficiency engines and intelligent energy management. For a compact SUV, fuel economy approaching hybrid-level figures will significantly reduce owners' running costs. The same day, NetEase Auto also published an interview with Changan Executive Vice President Jiang Ping, who emphasized that 'safety is not segmented by trim level,' calling for safety technology to be universally available across the entire model lineup — a clear statement of Changan's brand commitment to technology parity. Low fuel consumption combined with standard safety features across all trims forms Changan's core selling proposition in the mainstream SUV market.
articles.impact: The low real-world fuel consumption data provides strong endorsement for Blue Whale power and should help the Changan CS75 PLUS stay competitive in compact SUV sales rankings.

articles.title: Academician Ouyang Minggao: NEV Industry Accelerates Toward Smart, Low-Carbon Era
articles.summary: Academician Ouyang Minggao says intelligence and low-carbon goals are driving the global new energy vehicle industry to upgrade at a faster pace.
articles.detail: According to a report republished by Sogou News, Chinese Academy of Sciences Academician Ouyang Minggao has outlined the development direction of the new energy vehicle (NEV) industry, saying it is accelerating toward a new chapter of smart and low-carbon growth. Ouyang noted that electrification is only the first half of the game, and intelligence will bring deeper industrial transformation, with power batteries, electric drives, autonomous driving, and vehicle-road-cloud integration becoming the core of competition in the next stage. Globally, tighter EU carbon emission regulations and shifts in subsidy orientation under the US Inflation Reduction Act are pushing multiverse automakers to speed up their electrification transitions. Low-carbon development extends beyond product-level emissions to cover the entire value chain, including battery material recycling, green manufacturing, and supply chain carbon footprint management. Backed by a complete supply chain and a large market, China's NEV industry is moving from catching up to running abreast — and even leading.
articles.impact: The academician's remarks reinforce the smart and low-carbon theme, signaling that automakers' competitive focus is shifting from the electrification phase to smart technology and full-chain carbon management.

articles.title: Fierce Competition Shapes NEV Edge as Chinese Brands Go Global Faster
articles.summary: Intense domestic competition has forged the NEV industry's strengths, boosting the overseas expansion of Chinese brands.
articles.detail: According to Sogou News, fierce domestic market competition is seen as a key factor in shaping the competitive edge of China's NEV industry. In core areas such as batteries, motors, and electronic controls, companies like CATL and BYD have pushed cost and performance to world-leading levels through rapid technological iteration and scale effects. Meanwhile, Chinese automakers are stepping up global expansion: brands such as Chery, BYD, and MG are growing in Southeast Asia, Europe, and South America, with overseas plants and localized supply chains set to be a priority in the next stage. Challenges remain, including tariff barriers, adapting to local regulations, and weak brand recognition. The technological and cost dividends from competition are translating into pricing and product competitiveness for Chinese NEVs in international markets.
articles.impact: Domestic competition benefits are spilling over into overseas markets; Chinese NEV exports are likely to sustain growth, though trade barriers and localization challenges must be addressed.

articles.title: 25 Years of China's NEV Industry: Leap From Policy-Driven Growth to High-Quality Development
articles.summary: Xinhua In-depth reviews 25 years of China's NEV journey as the industry enters a new stage of high-quality development.
articles.detail: According to a Xinhua In-depth report republished by Sogou News, China's new energy vehicle industry has traversed a 25-year journey, leaping from policy-driven growth and subsidy support to market competition and high-quality development. Looking back, the 2009 "Ten Cities, One Thousand Vehicles" demonstration program laid the industry's foundation, followed by sustained market cultivation through purchase subsidies and tax exemptions; subsidy cuts in 2018 forced automakers to sharpen their technology and cost-control capabilities; after 2020, brands such as BYD, NIO and XPeng stood out in market competition, with output and sales ranking first globally for multiple consecutive years. The industry has now entered a new stage of high-quality development, with the core focus shifting from "whether we have it" to "whether it's good enough," involving deeper issues such as battery safety, autonomous driving regulations, used-car residual values and the balanced deployment of charging infrastructure. Twenty-five years of accumulation have given China's NEV sector a complete industry chain and deep talent reserves.
articles.impact: This industry retrospective offers lessons for the sector, signaling that the next phase of competition will hinge on quality, safety and systemic capabilities rather than mere scale expansion.

articles.title: Shandong Consumer Council Issues NEV Buying Guide as Purchasing Decisions Turn More Rational
articles.summary: Shandong Consumer Council releases a new NEV buying guide, offering consumers a reference for purchase decisions.
articles.detail: According to CNR News, the Shandong Provincial Consumer Council recently issued a new energy vehicle buying guide, providing consumers with systematic purchase recommendations across dimensions including real-world driving range, battery warranty policies, charging convenience, the practicality of smart features and after-sales service networks. The guide urges consumers to note the gap between CLTC-rated range and real-world performance, to clarify the specifics of battery degradation and warranty terms, and to choose between pure-electric and hybrid models based on daily commuting distances and charging conditions. The release of such a buying guide at the consumer council level reflects that NEV consumption has moved from an early-adopter phase to mass adoption, with users making more rational decisions and paying greater attention to total cost of ownership over the product lifecycle. Similar consumer guidance also helps rein in sales pitch practices and reduce disputes over inflated range claims and misleading feature specifications.
articles.impact: Authoritative consumer guidance will improve transparency in purchase decisions, pushing automakers to adopt more standardised marketing claims and after-sales practices.

articles.title: Guangzhou Auto Show Nears as New Models Launch Ahead of Year-End Sprint
articles.summary: New models including the Yijing X9 EV are set to debut at the Guangzhou Auto Show on November 27, intensifying year-end competition.
articles.detail: According to information reported by NetEase Auto, the Yijing X9 EV will officially launch at the Guangzhou Auto Show on November 27, while the Huajing S five-seat version has also been unveiled, featuring Huawei Qiankun intelligent driving technology and CATL battery cells as standard — showcasing the dense rollout of Huawei-ecosystem vehicles. Meanwhile, the Fangchengbao Tai 9 has opened pre-orders ahead of its planned launch, targeting the premium segment; Dongfeng Yipai, Stelato and other brands have also recently unveiled new vehicle moves. As the year's closing flagship show, the Guangzhou Auto Show has long been a key stage for automakers to debut new models, announce pre-sale prices and showcase technology milestones. With purchase-tax breaks and local trade-in subsidies still in effect, automakers are racing to capture the year-end consumption peak, and more models are expected to公布 pricing and delivery plans around the show.
articles.impact: A wave of new models landing around the Guangzhou Auto Show could stack year-end price wars on top of new-model battles, giving consumers more choices while sharpening market competition.

articles.title: Q4 Delivery Sprint Begins as EV Newcomers Face a New Round of Reshuffling
articles.summary: XPeng targets 170,000 deliveries in Q4 as the industry enters the critical year-end sales sprint.
articles.detail: NetEase Auto reports that XPeng expects Q4 deliveries to exceed 170,000, an upbeat forecast reflecting the entire new-energy vehicle industry's entry into the final delivery sprint of the year. Recent moves across automakers point in the same direction: NIO ES8 deliveries surpassing 160,000 units, the Fangchengbao Tai 9 opening pre-orders, the Stelato V8 entering the market at an aggressive price, and the Yijing X9 about to launch — all signaling a strategy of trading scale for market share and using new models to drive sales. Q4 has always been a peak consumption season, and with year-end subsidies and pre-Spring Festival purchase demand layered on top, automakers will pull out all the stops to hit annual targets. For consumers, this is a favorable window to buy — but they should also watch for delivery-quality fluctuations and after-sales pressure caused by volume-chasing. The final year-end sales rankings will be decided over the coming month and a half.
articles.impact: The year-end sprint will lift Q4 sales while deepening industry divergence, with delivery capability and service systems becoming the decisive variables in the rankings.
